Consult Summary:
- Patient with known heart failure reports 2 weeks of progressive shortness of breath, worse over the last few days, with new bilateral ankle swelling and mild dry cough; no chest pain or palpitations. Clinician suspects a heart failure flare-up; exam/vitals reportedly OK. Plan: increase furosemide temporarily, order blood tests and echocardiogram, follow up in 1 week, with safety-net advice.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Increasing shortness of breath.
- Timeline:
  - ~2 weeks: Gradual worsening dyspnea.
  - Last few days: Marked increase in breathlessness; now symptomatic with minimal exertion and around the house.
  - Last few days: New bilateral ankle swelling.
- Characteristics/associated symptoms:
  - Dyspnea on minimal exertion (previously able to walk to shops without symptoms).
  - Mild dry cough.
  - Feels a bit run-down.
  - No chest pain.
  - No palpitations.
  - No fever.
  - Appetite and oral intake normal.
  - Urinating frequently, attributed to diuretic use.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No chest pain, palpitations, or fevers.
- Patient concerns: Worried about worsening heart failure and impact on ability to work.

Past Medical History:
- Heart failure (date of diagnosis not specified). Prior similar episode with ankle swelling at initial diagnosis; previously improved on medication.
- History of “small heart attack” approximately 5 years ago; hospitalized for a few days; patient cannot recall specific diagnosis name; stated “more than angina.”

Medications:
- Furosemide: previously 1 tablet daily; plan to increase to 1 tablet twice daily for the next few days (dose in mg not documented; route/frequency otherwise not documented).
- Aspirin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Bisoprolol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives alone with two cats (Polly and Tim).
- Occupation: Part-time lorry (truck) driver; daytime shifts only; work can be exhausting; concerned about work if symptoms worsen.
- Tobacco: Former smoker; ~1 pack/day for ~25 years; quit.
- Alcohol: Does not drink alcohol.
- Exercise: Walks to the shops daily when able; no vigorous exercise currently.

Family History:
- Father: Died of heart attack in early 60s.
- Mother: Osteoporosis; alive.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Oxygen saturation and blood pressure reported as “OK”; specific values not documented.
- Respiratory/chest: Clinician reports chest examination “OK” (no further details).
- General: Otherwise well per clinician.

Investigations:
- Planned/ordered:
  - Blood tests: Full blood count (to assess for anemia) and kidney function.
  - Echocardiogram to assess cardiac function; expected scheduling in 1–2 weeks.
- No results available at this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Worsening dyspnea with bilateral ankle swelling in a patient with known heart failure — suspected acute decompensation/flare-up.
  - Increase furosemide from 1 tablet daily to 1 tablet twice daily for the next few days (dose in mg not documented).
  - Order blood tests: full blood count and kidney function.
  - Arrange echocardiogram within 1–2 weeks.
  - Follow-up appointment in ~1 week to reassess symptoms and review results/orders.
  - Safety-netting: Seek earlier review if worsening breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.

- Issue 2: History of prior “small heart attack” (~5 years ago).
  - Continue current secondary prevention noted (aspirin, beta-blocker) — specific doses not documented.
  - Further characterization of past event may be informed by records; not addressed in this consult.

- General Plan items:
  - Patient agrees with plan.
  - Advise to monitor symptoms and contact clinician sooner if deterioration occurs.

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected elements:
  - No vital sign values documented (BP, HR, RR, SpO2 numbers absent).
  - No weight, orthopnea/PND history, or recent weight change documentation.
  - Medication doses, routes, and frequencies (except adjusted furosemide schedule) not documented.
  - No baseline or prior echocardiogram results or ejection fraction noted.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Brief confusion between metoprolol vs bisoprolol; patient confirmed bisoprolol (conflict resolved).
  - “Two tablets a day” vs “one tablet twice a day” stated; both indicate total of two tablets daily (no conflict).
- Transcript quality:
  - Minor connection issues and conversational pauses; clinically adequate information captured.
